history.dynasty: None attested; legend speaks of King Jholan of ancient Jakhapur
history.period: Ancient (legendary; tradition traces it to Treta Yuga); exact construction date unknown
history.summary: The Shri Mahalakshmi Jagdamba Mandir at Koradi, popularly called the Koradi Devi Temple, is the most celebrated Mahalaxmi shrine in the Nagpur region and is regarded by devotees as one of the 51 Shakti-peeths (verify - this is a devotional claim, not epigraphically established). Legend says the place was once Jakhapur, ruled by King Jholan, who after long penance was blessed with a daughter in whom he recognised Adi Shakti; the girl, called Jakhumai, led his army to victory and then halted to rest at Jakhapur as the sun set, disappearing and leaving a self-manifested (swayambhu) idol of Mahalakshmi Jagdamba in her place. The goddess is worshipped in three forms through the day - as a young girl in the morning, a youthful woman in the afternoon, and an elderly woman at night - and devotees report a solar phenomenon in which the setting sun's rays fall on the idol on certain days in March and September (verify). She is the Kuldevi (family deity) of the Vidarbha community. The temple complex has been extensively renovated in recent decades and now includes a Ramayana museum/centre. Ambiguity note: the CSV lists this temple at town 'Nagpur'; that matches the famous Koradi shrine, but a separate, 100+-year-old Mahalaxmi Devasthan also exists inside Nagpur city at Kelibag Road, Mahal (open roughly 6 AM-1 PM and 4-9:30 PM per visitor reports), which may be what some listings mean by 'Mahalaxmi Temple, Nagpur'.

name: Shri Mahalaxmi Devi Temple
town_description: Nagpur, the 'Orange City' of Maharashtra, is a major commercial and transport hub in the Vidarbha region, famous for its oranges, the Deekshabhoomi Buddhist monument, and its position at the geographical centre of India. The Shri Mahalaxmi Devi Temple most commonly identified with Nagpur is the Koradi temple, about 13-15 km north of the city centre on the banks of Koradi Lake; Koradi itself is a small temple town also known for the Koradi Thermal Power Station.

travel.airport: Dr. Babasaheb Ambedkar International Airport, Nagpur (approx. 21-27 km; taxis and app cabs available).
travel.railway: Nagpur Junction Railway Station (approx. 13-15 km), well connected across India.
travel.road: About 13-15 km north of Nagpur city centre at Koradi (Nagpur-441111); buses run from Sitabardi Bus Stand (Morbhavan) to the temple, plus autos, taxis and cabs. The temple is on the banks of Koradi Lake, near the Nagpur-Bhopal highway.

visitor_information.best_time: October to March for pleasant weather. Navratri (September-October) is the grandest time but draws very large crowds; weekday mornings and late evenings are quietest.
visitor_information.opening_hours: Roughly 6:00 AM to 9:00/10:00 PM daily (verify - listings vary between 6 AM-9 PM and 6 AM-10 PM). Entry is free. Dress modestly (traditional attire recommended), remove footwear at the designated stand, and confirm photography rules with temple staff before clicking pictures inside.
